instrument_name: DRS Informational Publication 2026(1) Connecticut Employer's Tax Guide (Circular CT)
article_or_section: Q5 (gross CT wages); 'Residents working outside CT' (proration among qualifying jurisdictions); '15-Day Rule for Nonresident Employees' p.8; CT-W4NA allocation
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident employees: CT wages = all wages regardless of where services performed; where employer must withhold for another state, CT tax is prorated and only the excess remitted (Example 4). Nonresidents: CT wages = wages for services performed in CT, allocated on CT-W4NA; 15-day rule: no withholding if 15 days or less in CT in the calendar year, but if more than 15 days, withhold on all CT-service pay including the first 15 days (PS 2015(6)). No reciprocity agreement appears anywhere in IP 2026(1) (full-text search 'reciproc': none).

instrument_name: Oregon DOR 150-206-692 Withholding/Transit Tax Information: Out-of-state/Nonresident Employers (current edition Rev. 02-08-22)
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer withholds from resident and nonresident employees working in Oregon. Out-of-state employers of OR residents working in OR: withhold on all wages incl. telecommuting; may be relieved if each employee gets 300 or less per year. Employer with no employees working in OR: withholding for OR residents cannot be required (requested as convenience). Nonresidents: withhold on wages for OR services unless OR earnings for the year will be less than the standard deduction for their filing status (amount changes yearly; 2026 amount 2,910 single per US-OR-P5-1-002). No reciprocity agreement stated (full-text search 'recipro': none). Transit taxes TriMet/LTD apply regardless of residence.
